newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF's Knoll and IVAX Corp cease joint venture.
newsitem.headline: BASF's Knoll and IVAX Corp cease joint venture.

text.p: Pharmaceutical group Knoll AG, a unit of German chemical giant BASF AG, said on Friday it had ended a joint venture with U.S. drug company IVAX Corp to market generic pharmaceutical products in Germany.

The two groups have replaced the joint venture with a new alliance which gives Knoll exclusive and semi-exclusive marketing rights in Germany and semi-exclusive marketing rights in another twelve European countries to over 70 generic drugs and to certain proprietary drug products.

IVAX will receive royalties on net sales of the licensed products and has transferred its interest in the joint venture to Knoll. The joint venture was started in March 1995, Knoll said in a statement.

The alliance allows Knoll and IVAX to independently launch their own versions of the licensed products in any of the twelve countries in question, except Germany where Knoll has exclusive rights to certain of the licensed products, Knoll said.

Thorlef Spickschen, head of BASF's pharma division and chairman of Knoll AG, said: "The broad portfolio of generic products licensed to us by IVAX, along with the potential of our own patented melt extrusion manufacturing technology, allows Knoll to advance on our European generic drug operations."
